target_customer: Parents and kids who play mobile games, buying plush toy controllers through ZowPow's online store
problem: Mobile games are played on a flat screen. ZowPow put sensors in plush toys so a child could control gameplay physically.
business_model: Consumer hardware sold direct online, with a revenue share paid to the game developer on each toy sold

founders.name: Jennifer Lu
previous_startups: Started a gaming studio (no outcome given)
founders.background_notes: YC interview says she managed developer relations at OpenFeint and led business development and marketing at TinyCo. The YC company page lists her as Jennifer Bronzo (Doorstead co-founder and COO), apparently the same person under a later name; this identity link is an inference.

founders.name: Brian Krejcarek
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. The YC interview says the co-founder Brian previously worked with sensors and wireless technology.

competitors.name: PhoneJoy Play
competitors.what: Expandable Bluetooth gamepad for phones and tablets, crowdfunded
competitors.traction_then: Raised $69,859 on Kickstarter against a $50,000 goal

competitors.name: Flipside
competitors.what: Controller case for iPhone, iPad and other devices
competitors.traction_then: Second crowdfunding attempt after iOS 7 gamepad support

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to combine sensors, Bluetooth LE firmware, plush manufacturing and game SDK integration. Each part is standard, but hardware manufacturing is hard for two people.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed game partnerships were the only edge named. The hardware was copyable and depended on a few game partners.

incumbents: Skylanders and other toys to life makers
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acting against ZowPow. The company went inactive without public explanation.

market_need_then: Parents and game studios were interested in physical toys tied to mobile games, and the launch was timed for Christmas 2013. No independent demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Exact zowpow.com. The domain did not resolve when fetched.

identity.mascot_or_character: Plush toys of licensed game characters such as Redford and a tiny plane
identity.visual_style: Soft plush toys aimed at kids

branding.brand_signature: Plush toy controllers for licensed game characters
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch and Ubergizmo covered the December 2013 launch; no community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A playful onomatopoeic name with some launch press, but no sign of lasting awareness.

outcome_analysis: ZowPow launched plush toy controllers for mobile games in December 2013 and joined YC in the Winter 2014 batch as a two person team. No post mortem, shutdown notice or acquisition was found, so the cause of the company going inactive is not public. The failure factors listed are inferences from the narrow licensed game niche and consumer hardware economics, not statements from the founders.
notes: Funding sources conflict: Bounce Watch reports a $120K seed from Y Combinator dated March 2014 and CB Insights reports $20K total with ACE & Company and Y Combinator. Each rests on a single database, and the two entries may describe the same money; do not sum them. A YC blog post calls ZowPow W13 while the YC directory says Winter 2014; the TechCrunch article of December 2013 says it was accepted into the upcoming batch, consistent with Winter 2014. The company did not state the cause of inactivity. The company site did not resolve when fetched.
